job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today I learned so much about India's space missions! My teacher explained that Mangalyaan, or the Mars Orbiter Mission, was a brilliant success. Unlike what some think, it did not carry a rover to drive on the surface, nor did it land on Mars. Instead, it was an orbiter designed to study the Martian atmosphere and surface features from space. To reach Mars, it performed complex manoeuvres, firing its engines to slow down so it could be captured by Mars's gravity. It did not just float there; gravity exists everywhere in space, and it is what keeps satellites in their orbits. Later, we discussed Aditya-L1, our mission to study the Sun. It is not going to land on the Sun, which would be impossible due to the heat. Instead, it travels to a special point called L1, where the gravitational forces of the Sun and Earth interact to allow a stable halo orbit. It takes about four months to reach this point, not just a few days. Aditya-L1 carries seven different scientific instruments to observe the Sun's corona and solar winds, proving it is much more than just a simple camera. It is amazing how ISRO achieves these feats with such precision and planning!

items.evidence: To reach Mars, it performed complex manoeuvres, firing its engines to slow down so it could be captured by Mars's gravity.
items.q: Why did Mangalyaan have to fire its engines as it came near Mars?
options: To lose speed so Mars's gravity could capture it
To gain speed, since firing only makes things faster
To land gently on the surface of Mars
To steer, while Mars pulled it in by itself
items.explain: Mangalyaan fired its engines to slow down, so that Mars's gravity could capture it into orbit.

wrong.why: thinks engines can only speed a spacecraft up
thinks Mars pulled it in without any slowing down

items.evidence: It did not just float there; gravity exists everywhere in space, and it is what keeps satellites in their orbits.
items.q: A satellite keeps circling Earth for many years. What keeps it on its path?
options: Earth's gravity, which reaches out into space
Its height, which puts it beyond Earth's gravity
Its engines, which keep firing all the time
Empty space, where objects simply float freely
items.explain: Gravity exists everywhere in space, and it is gravity that keeps satellites moving in their orbits.

wrong.why: thinks satellites stay up because they are beyond gravity
thinks a spacecraft needs constant engine power to stay moving
thinks there is no gravity in space so things just float

items.evidence: Instead, it was an orbiter designed to study the Martian atmosphere and surface features from space.
items.q: How did Mangalyaan gather information about Mars?
options: By circling Mars and observing it from above
By driving a rover across its rocky ground
By landing and digging into its soil
By testing its rockets, without doing any science
items.explain: Mangalyaan was an orbiter: it went around Mars and studied its atmosphere and surface from space.

wrong.why: thinks the mission only proved technology, with no science

items.evidence: Instead, it travels to a special point called L1, where the gravitational forces of the Sun and Earth interact to allow a stable halo orbit.
items.q: What makes the point L1 a good place for Aditya-L1 to stay?
options: It is where Sun and Earth's pulls work together
It is where the Sun is cool enough to land
It is where the Moon and Earth's weather are seen
It is where no gravity acts, so it floats
items.explain: At L1 the gravity of the Sun and Earth interact, which lets Aditya-L1 stay in a stable halo orbit.

wrong.why: thinks Aditya-L1 is going to land on the Sun
thinks Aditya-L1 studies the Moon and Earth's weather
thinks there is no gravity in space

items.evidence: Aditya-L1 carries seven different scientific instruments to observe the Sun's corona and solar winds, proving it is much more than just a simple camera.
items.q: Why does Aditya-L1 carry seven instruments instead of just one camera?
options: To study different parts of the Sun, like its winds
To photograph the Moon and track Earth's weather
To show off India's skill, not to do science
To land on the Sun and measure its heat
items.explain: Its seven scientific instruments observe different things, such as the Sun's corona and solar winds, so it is more than a camera.

wrong.why: thinks Aditya-L1 studies the Moon and Earth's weather
thinks space missions only prove technology
thinks Aditya-L1 will land on the Sun
